retrospective.harder_than_needed: AC-DECLINE-12's deferral gate turned out to require real cross-mechanism plumbing: subscribeToWelcomes (kind-1059, once per identity) and subscribeToGroupMessages (kind-445, once per group) are independent async flows in the SAME module with no existing signal between them, so I had to add a module-level per-groupId sync-completion Set/waiter-Map purely to let a decline defer until ITS specific group's historical sync completes, then thread that same signal through every OTHER decline test's setup (since applyDecline unconditionally awaits the sync gate, an un-synced groupId hangs the test forever) — a non-obvious cross-cutting test-fixture requirement that only became visible after the first full test run hung/failed. Getting a reliable (non-flaky) test for the two-genuinely-concurrent-declines regression also took real thought: a static mock member-list can't distinguish serialized from unserialized behavior, so the deps fixture needed to be genuinely stateful (commit() mutates a real array) with a deterministic macrotask-level delay, not a microtask-count guess.
retrospective.surprised_by: A same-story TypeScript check surfaced a real generic-inference mismatch: MarmotContext.tsx's init() closes over a freshly-constructed `client` (typed with its inferred mediaFactory generics), and passing its `.groups.get()` result into the existing sendRumorSafe(group: MarmotGroupType, ...) helper does not typecheck — every other Deps-building callback in the file sidesteps this by reading clientRef.current (typed MarmotClient<undefined,undefined>) instead of the local `client` const, a convention that isn't documented anywhere and that I only found by comparing against cancelPendingInvitation's own dep-building callback.

notes.dd7_ordering_implementation: welcomeSubscription.ts's new INVITE_DECLINE_KIND dispatch branch (slotted after the join-request 21059 branch, before the kind-444 guard) authenticates the seal first (AC-DECLINE-8), extracts ONLY `groupId` from the decline payload (never trusting the payload's self-claimed `pubkey` field — the actor is always unwrapResult.pubkey, lowercased), then calls a new module-private `applyDecline(groupId, pubkeyLower, deps)` helper wrapped in a per-(groupId,pubkey) serialization chain (`runSerializedDeclineProcessing`, mirroring pendingDirectInviteStorage.ts's consumePendingDirectInviteMarker chain pattern). `applyDecline` awaits `waitForGroupHistorySync(groupId)` (DD-10 deferral, see below), re-checks `isPendingMemberImpl` (DD-4, re-checked post-defer rather than cached from dispatch time), then calls `cancelPendingInvitationImpl(deps, groupId, pubkeyLower, sendAnnouncement, 'declined')` — a NEW optional 5th param on the existing S9(invite-rescind epic)/ADR-010 Remove-machinery function, defaulted to 'invite_cancelled' so the pre-existing admin Cancel-Invite/Remove-Member flow is byte-for-byte unchanged. That single call performs steps (1) Remove-commit and (2) post SEQUENTIALLY inside its own existing body (already-established ordering, unmodified). On `{ok:true}`, applyDecline then runs step (3) `clearPendingDirectInvite(groupId, pubkeyLower)` (best-effort, caught), and returns true, on which the dispatch marks the gift wrap seen (step 4) — the ONLY point localStorage's processedGiftWraps key is touched for this branch. A Remove-commit failure (`{ok:false}`) short-circuits before step 2/3, and mark-seen never happens, so the whole sequence reprocesses on next start (verified via a dedicated commit-throws test).
notes.deferral_mechanism: Two NEW module-level singletons in welcomeSubscription.ts: `historySyncedGroupIds: Set<string>` and `historySyncWaiters: Map<string, Array<() => void>>`. `subscribeToGroupMessages`'s existing historical-sync-complete check now ALSO calls `markGroupHistorySynced(groupId)` unconditionally (regardless of whether the caller supplied its own onHistorySynced callback), which resolves any pending waiters for that groupId and adds it to the synced set. `applyDecline` awaits `waitForGroupHistorySync(groupId)`, which resolves immediately if already synced or registers a one-shot resolver otherwise. This is explicitly NOT a new unbounded queue: each groupId has at most one waiter-list entry, drained and removed the moment its group syncs; a group that never syncs this session simply leaves its decline(s) pending in-memory for that session's lifetime, falling back to the pre-existing unmarked-gift-wrap reprocessing on next app start (DD-7 guarantee #3) if the process exits first.
notes.converging_two_genuine_declines: Per-(groupId, lowercased-pubkey) serialization via `runSerializedDeclineProcessing`, a promise-chain map identical in structure to pendingDirectInviteStorage.ts's consumePendingDirectInviteMarker chain: a second decline for the same key awaits the FIRST call's entire applyDecline (sync-wait through marker-clear) before its own tree-gate check even begins, so it always observes the post-Remove state and no-ops. Verified by a dedicated adversarial test with a STATEFUL mock (commit() mutates a real shared member-list array, gated by a real 30ms macrotask delay so the race window is deterministically observable regardless of NIP-59 crypto timing) firing two DISTINCT-outer-eventId gift wraps concurrently (Promise.all, no await between the two fireEvent calls) and asserting exactly one commit/post/marker-clear.
notes.architecture_doc_gap_observed: architecture.md's Order-Sensitive Composition section lists decline-a/decline-b/cancelInvitationImpl.ts as the flow's participating modules but does not explicitly name pendingDirectInviteStorage.ts, despite DD-10 guarantee #1 explicitly requiring a marker-clear step. Not a conflict for this story (the marker-clear capability is consumed via injection at the MarmotContext.tsx composition root, matching this codebase's established boundary-rule convention — never a direct import into welcomeSubscription.ts/cancelInvitationImpl.ts), but flagged here as a minor spec-completeness observation for whoever next revises architecture.md, not escalated as a blocking finding.
